svg.aria-label: Secondary succession timeline in six steps: mature forest; disturbance (fire) - soil stays; 0 to 1 year, immediate aftermath - survivors include large trees and some animals, with a seed bank in the soil; 1 to 20 years, early recovery - grasses and wildflowers (pioneers); 20 to 150 years, mid-recovery - shrubs and small trees; 150 plus years, long-term recovery (climax). A soil layer stays intact under every step. Contrast note: primary succession starts with no soil.
svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Secondary succession timeline after a fire
svg.text: Secondary succession: recovery after a disturbance (soil stays)
SOIL STAYS INTACT the whole way (seed bank + roots survive)
Contrast: Primary succession starts with NO soil (bare rock).
Secondary succession starts with soil already in place, so it is faster.
